set.body:
Follow-ups from the cold review of 4b (5ec21c243..ac4b42a96; fixes at 173343bdc). None blocks landing.
1. Overwritten and stray answers leave no trace (AgentReplay.answered, AgentAnswers.participant): a unit answered twice (last wins), a reply item for an index outside the unit table (dropped), and a unit answered by a chunk other than its own are not counted or flagged. processing.chunk means "own chunk" for omitted/unparsable and "answering chunk" for answered. Record counts in the receipt and a flag on the unit row.
2. Confidence goes through toDouble, unlike alternative p (kept as Json): 1e-400 becomes Value(0.0). Keep the reported number verbatim.
3. Scene range is the scene count (correct only while scenes are numbered 1..N contiguously); AgentArmImport.SceneCount is hard-coded 50 while the bundle uses atlas.scenes.size. Take the valid scene numbers from the source.
4. Bundle size: ~9 MB per participant because each record embeds the full source description. Consider one shared source section.
5. The film loader and inventory recipe are Sherlock-specific (SherlockAnnotations.Atlas, "sherlock-recall" title). FilmFestival should drive the generalisation.
6. No test covers the @main command path end to end (it calls sys.exit); binding is now tested through AgentMappingRecord.bind.
7. read_bundle.py does not verify recordDigest or provenance; the Scala reader reads provenance and the source dictionary as written.
Done in the fix commits: text-checked unit binding (B1), Python test import path (B2), parity receipt (B3), Scala reader slot/row agreement, Python unit accounting, per-field counts receipt, named-model provider identity with recall hash as an input, discriminating edited-record test, edge tests, doc corrections.
set.title: Step 4b follow-ups: overwritten/stray answers, verbatim confidence, scene numbering, bundle size, generalise loader
